bullets.title: S&P posts strongest session since March; NDX best day since June on broad AI rally
bullets.body: S&P 500 finished +2.3% with breadth 6:1 positive (strongest since Nov 2025), while NDX surged +3.4% with semis +6.9%. The rally was broad-based despite NVDA's -5% drag, with unprofitable tech, semis ex-NVDA, and energy alternative names leading. JPM reiterates YE26 SPX target of 8,000 (8.4% upside from Friday) based on $365 EPS at 21.9x.

bullets.title: JPM flags 10 bullish catalysts: clean positioning, oversold RSIs, AI multiple compression
bullets.body: JPM cites RSI at 30 on NDX, AI multiples compressed 35% since May (Semis -52%, Memory -60%), levered ETF exposure below Jan 2026 levels, and ~$50B CTA selling remaining as a dwindling headwind. Bond yields are expected to shift from negative to positive interpretation as they peak, with value-vs-growth rotation underway.

bullets.title: 22V and UBS confirm near-term risk-on setup; CTA positioning at bottoming signal
bullets.body: 22V revised near-term outlook toward lower VIX and risk-on outperformance following financial conditions tightening, while longer-term AI and inflation risks persist. UBS notes Risk Control Exposure at 55% (lowest since Tariff period) and CTA Equity Exposure at -5%, flagging negative CTA positioning as a bottoming signal; UBS forecasts SPX to grind +10% higher over next three months.

bullets.title: NVDA -5% on CEO Huang espionage scandal; succession risk flagged as major overhang
bullets.body: NVDA fell 5% after CEO Jensen Huang admitted an affair with a woman US intelligence deemed a Chinese spy, triggering an internal company investigation and Commerce Dept referral to DoJ. Analysts and investors flagged NVDA's lack of succession planning as a key risk, though prediction markets show low probability of Huang's departure and major investors are rallying to support him.

bullets.title: AI trade decouples from NVDA: semis ex-NVDA +6.9%, software outperforms semis by 400bps
bullets.body: The AI rally continued despite NVDA headlines, with AMD surging +13.3% on an Oppenheimer upgrade, GOOGL introducing new TPU 8tx/8i Max chips, and META +5.1% ahead of its monetization meeting. UBS AI Winners basket gained +5.1%, and software outperformed semis by over 400bps intraday, suggesting rotation within the AI trade from hardware toward software and infrastructure.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley: AI capex cycle intact post-midterms; 'Buy the Drop' across hyperscalers and infrastructure
bullets.body: MS argues midterm election impact on data center capex is overblown — only ~20% of US projects shift from 2028 to 2029, while global additions accelerate +20% YoY in 2029 and hyperscaler capex forecasts remain at $1.6T/$1.8T in 2027/2028. MS recommends buying AMZN, META, GOOGL, MSFT, NVDA, AVGO, EQIX, WULF, CEG, VST, TLN, GEV, ANET, STX, WDC on reset valuations; a >30% powered data center shortfall through 2028 favors the best-capitalized players.

bullets.title: Data center REITs +3.83%; Cantor, Wells Fargo, Morgan Stanley all recommend buying the dip
bullets.body: Data Center REITs outperformed the S&P (+2.35%) with Cantor maintaining overweight on EQIX, DLR, HUT, WULF, NBIS, CRWV and characterizing the selloff as a significant overreaction. Wells Fargo sees FY27 capacity mostly insulated, while Morgan Stanley favors EQIX and powered shell providers (WULF, HUT, APLD). DLR and Goodman Group also acquired a 9.9% stake in NextDC (~$500M) for APAC expansion.

bullets.title: Nuclear/SMR and energy IPO names surge; oil -4.4% on US-Iran deal reports
bullets.body: Energy IPO basket gained 9% (best day since July) with SMR names up 30%+ over recent days; OKLO +14%, NNE +12.3%, CEG +10.5% on alternative energy demand for data centers. Meanwhile WTI fell below $90/barrel (-4.4%) on reports of a possible US-Iran diplomatic deal, and the oil-Treasury yield correlation has turned negative.

bullets.title: CPI preview: JPM expects Oct core 0.23% m/m, sees 10yr yields ~14bp too low
bullets.body: JPM forecasts October core CPI at 0.23% m/m (vs. consensus 0.08% and market pricing 0.21%), noting September beat expectations by 7bp — the largest upside surprise since March 2024. 10-year yields are estimated ~14bp too low after controlling for Fed/inflation/growth factors; tomorrow's $42bn 10-year auction is expected to require a concession. Market is pricing ~80% chance of a December hike with 43bp of hikes through end of next year.

bullets.title: Piper Sandler and PSC expect tame Oct CPI headline; disinflation to push y/y to 1-handle by 2Q27
bullets.body: PSC forecasts Oct CPI at 0.2% m/m headline and core, citing falling gasoline prices (futures point to $3.60/gal in 1H27), accelerating core goods disinflation (-1.5% y/y Adobe basket), and NAND prices down 20% from 2026 highs. Headline CPI could drop to a 1-handle y/y by 2Q27 from 3.7% in September; CPI housing inflation continuing a glacial slowdown with rent/OER expected to track closer to 2%.

bullets.title: Rent inflation re-normalizing per Zillow ZORI; don't fade official CPI shelter data
bullets.body: Zillow's ZORI 3-month rate held at 4.25% for a second consecutive month and 6-month rate returned to its pre-Covid midpoint of 4%, suggesting the lead from marginal rents has run its course. The 12-month ZORI rate is now 2.9% and rising, implying official government shelter measures should be taken at face value — rents are over-weighted in CPI by a factor of more than 2.

bullets.title: ARM cloud instances surge +11% m/m as NVDA Pascal phases out; broad server demand strengthening
bullets.body: KeyBanc Cloud Instance Tracker shows ARM instances +11% m/m (+43% y/y) driven by Google Axion +26% m/m and Azure Cobalt +15% m/m, while NVDA instances fell -6% m/m as Pascal dropped 34% at GCP/BABA with Blackwell only +1% m/m. Overall cloud instances +2% m/m/+12% y/y with traditional server demand strengthening; analysts view ARM, AMD, INTC, MU implications as positive and NVDA neutral.

bullets.title: Citi TMT Hardware Roundtable: bullish on DELL/CSCO/ANET post-correction; AI capex risk in H2 2027+
bullets.body: Roundtable participants see DELL's near-term guidance as conservative with improved setup post-correction, CSCO with potential for hyperscaler guidance upside from $7.5B to $8B+, and ANET slightly preferred over CLS on valuation. Key risk flagged: potential H2 2027/2028 capex cuts from regulatory impacts, hardware cycle roll-over, and lack of discovery potential at current elevated expectations.

bullets.title: JPM Asia strategy: AI stocks oversold at <10th percentile positioning; buy non-AI for near-term diversification
bullets.body: Asian equities fell ~15% on a rolling monthly basis with tech RSIs in the early 20s and Price Momentum factor correcting 45% from June highs — nearly matching 1998-99 and 2009 drawdowns. JPM sees no signs of AI cycle end but recommends near-term diversification into uncorrelated non-AI sectors (Financials, Healthcare, Energy, Staples, Telecom, Utilities) while remaining thematically bullish on AI.

bullets.title: Piper Sandler midday: Tech/Semi leadership has failed technically; Healthcare and Staples now leading
bullets.body: Piper Sandler flags that Technology and Semiconductor leadership has broken down on absolute and relative strength, with Healthcare and Consumer Staples taking leadership. Investors are advised to reduce exposure to failed Tech trends and watch S&P 500 support at 7,325–7,314; medium-term concern that GOP/Trump policy aggressiveness poses near-term economy and market downside risk.

bullets.title: TTD surges 23% after-hours on massive earnings beat and $731M buyback authorization
bullets.body: Trade Desk reported Q3 revenue of $736M (+13% vs guidance/consensus) and adj. EBITDA of $265.8M (36.1% margin, +65% vs consensus), with Q4 revenue guidance of at least $755M (+10% vs consensus) and adj. EBITDA of at least $280M (+45% vs consensus). The board approved an additional $731M buyback bringing total available to $1B; Citi maintains a Sell/$11 PT despite the beat, citing macro headwinds, management changes, and DSP competition.

bullets.title: Taiwan Oct exports +58.9% y/y to record $94B confirms AI supply chain strength
bullets.body: Taiwan's October export data surged 58.9% year-over-year to a record $94B, driven by AI supply chain demand, corroborating the fundamental case for the AI infrastructure buildout despite recent equity volatility in semiconductor names.

bullets.title: Anthropic targeting $1.2-1.5T IPO valuation pre-Thanksgiving; TeraWulf secures Google credit backstop for $19B Anthropic lease
bullets.body: Anthropic is advancing IPO plans with a targeted $1.2-1.5T valuation ahead of Thanksgiving, while TeraWulf secured a Google credit backstop supporting a $19B Anthropic data center lease. Separately, fal-Features & Labels raised $1.3B backed by NVIDIA and T. Rowe Price, and Shield AI raised $2B from JPMorgan and Blackstone, underscoring continued private AI capital formation.

bullets.title: Fox completes Roku acquisition; ROKU delisted from NASDAQ
bullets.body: Fox Corp (FOXA) closed its acquisition of Roku on November 6, 2026, with ROKU shares delisted from NASDAQ. UBS and Wolfe Research both ceased coverage; prior estimates implied FY2026E revenue of $5.77B and adjusted EBITDA of $810M.

bullets.title: Fed's Goolsbee: consumer spending driving growth but Fed has failed to address inflation
bullets.body: Fed Governor Goolsbee stated that consumer spending has been the main growth driver while acknowledging the Fed has failed to adequately address inflation. Markets are pricing approximately 80% probability of a December rate hike with 43bp of additional hikes priced through end of next year.
